title: Clear your desk into a trash can another robot arm is also using
instruction: Put the paper ball, the tin and the wrapper from the green mat into the trash can.
context: People sharing one bin, sink or printer wait for the other to finish before they reach in. This checks that a policy can use a shared trash can whose mouth takes one hand at a time, beside a second arm that is using it too and cannot be talked to.
setup: A 90 x 90 cm wooden table top, 75 cm high. Two YAM arms stand side by side at the back edge, 50 cm apart; the controlled arm is the right one in the screenshot. Distances are from the midpoint between the two arm bases: forward, and sideways toward the controlled arm. A dark grey trash can, 15 x 15 cm inside and 9 cm deep, 30 cm forward on the centre line. A green 20 x 20 cm desk mat 31 cm forward and 28 cm toward the controlled arm, and a blue one the same toward the other arm. On each: a white 3.2 cm paper cube (60 g), a grey tin 3 cm across and 4 cm tall standing on end (60 g), and an orange 3 x 5.2 x 2.4 cm wrapper lying flat (70 g). The other arm clears the blue mat into the can, keeping its hand away from the can's mouth while the controlled arm's hand is there. It does the same in every trial.
scoring: The share of the three pieces from the green mat that are inside the trash can (within its walls, below its rim) at the end. 0 if the two arms ever touch; the run stops at the first touch, and 1 s after all three are in the can.
reset_notes: Take all six pieces out of the can and put them back on their mats, as in the screenshot.
fidelity: Approximate. The rubbish is rigid blocks and a cylinder with torsional friction, not crumpled paper or a dented tin. Arm links collide as fitted capsules slightly larger than the real ones, so a near miss under about 1 cm can count as a touch. The gripper pinches with up to 50 N through flat pads. The controller uses the manufacturer's joint gains, gravity compensation and motor torque-speed limits. The other arm is scripted on the true scene state.
